text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Steel producer VSZ expects to post an unconsolidated net profit of around 1.3 billion crowns for 1996, some 100 million crowns more than in 1995.

- According to a language law that became effective from the beginning of this year, legal entities can be fined with 50,000 to 500,000 crowns for improper use of the state language. The law will, for example, reduce the usage of the foreign words in advertisements.
- If Slovakia joined NATO, some 54 percent of Slovak citizens would not agree with dispatching of the Slovak army forces in another NATO member country, according to an oppinion poll.
- The official Slovak Television will be granted some 312 million crowns from the state budget this year, up from 175 million crowns in 1996, to cover its operating costs.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The deliveries of Russian crude oil through the Druzhba pipeline continue without any interruption according to an agreed schedule, oil refiner Slovnaft said.
- The state fund of market regulation will have at its disposal some 1.5 billion crowns this year to subsidise export agricultural production.
- Slovakia's sole shipbuilder Slovenske Lodenice a.s. in 1996 met its target completing 16 cargo vessels, with the production totalling some 3.5 billion crowns.
- Sales of processed and unprocessed wood totalled 2.9 billion crowns in the first three quarters of last year, some 6.1 percent less than in the same period last year.
- Slovakia's only producer of tobacco products S.I.T. increased prices by an average six percent from the beginning of this year.

SME - The Czech secret service has strictly rejected allegations by the Slovak daily Slovenska Republika, a pro-government newspaper, that it was involved in the kidnapping of the Slovak president's son in 1995.
- According to a public opinion poll carried out by the U.S. information agency, some 72 percent of Slovak citizens support the idea of integration to the European Union.

PRAVDA - The minimum price for the privatisation bonds is, from the beginning of this year, 8,160 crowns - the guaranteed 75 percent of the nominal value plus the annual yield, set at the central bank's discont rate (8.8 percent).
At the end of last year, the o-t-c bourse registered more than 160,000 orders to sell the bonds for last year's minimum price of 7,500 crowns.
